text:
maya: FYI — large hosted customer reporting recurring tool-call failures when passing binary attachments via the Python SDK. Error shows arg parsing failure and payload appears truncated at a null byte. They've seen a billing spike from automatic retries. Repro steps below.
maya: repro (python 0.14.2):
```py
from redwood import Client
c = Client(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_KEY'])
# payload contains embedded null bytes
payload = b"header\x00\x01payload\x00trailer"
c.call_tool('file_inspect', { 'data': payload })
```
maya: API response: `{"error":"invalid_tool_args","message":"arg parsing failed at offset 7"}`
devin: can you paste request headers and sdk versions? is this hosted or dedicated? any proxy in front?
maya: Hosted API, no customer proxy. SDKs used: py 0.14.2, ts 1.9.0, go v0.9.0. I attached minimal repro payload and server error above. support-bot: created INC-1234 and linked customer ticket.
support-bot: ticket INC-1234 created and assigned to support oncall
samir: quick guess — we recently added a framing sentinel for raw bytes during tool serialisation. If SDKs inconsistently encode/decode null bytes it could truncate at first 0x00. Does python vs ts behave differently if you pass base64 vs raw bytes?
maya: interesting — python -> base64 path seems OK if we manually base64 encode before call. Typescript and Go customers reported corruption unless they pass a string. Example (ts):
```ts
const payload = Buffer.from([0x68,0x00,0x01,0x02]);
client.callTool('file_inspect', { data: payload }); // observed truncation
// workaround:
client.callTool('file_inspect', { data: payload.toString('base64') });
```
irene: can we capture wire-level to confirm actual bytes hitting API? eli, can eng-runtime confirm whether API layer treats 0x00 as terminator for tool args?
eli: putting on eng-runtime. I suspect a codec mismatch in the JSON marshalling step where some SDKs hand off a Buffer that ends up being toString()'d implicitly. I'll try a tcpdump and also reproduce locally with our hosted endpoint. Assigning P0 label.
devin: customer also logged latency complaints because client retries on failure. Support: propose immediate credit and advise base64 workaround until patched.
samir: probable root cause: TS/Go SDK call path uses `bytes` -> JSON string conversion that strips NULs if intermediate conversion uses C string APIs in one of our helper libs. Python path encodes explicitly to base64 by default which is why it was okay in that case.
eli: action items:
- eng-runtime: reproduce and add unit test for NUL-containing payloads across SDKs (owner: eli)
- eng-ml/serving: harden API decoder to accept explicit base64 marker and raw bytes framing (owner: samir)
- SDK teams: roll patch to explicit base64 encode or signal framing flag (owners: ts-sdk team, go-sdk team)
- support: offer one-time billing credit and notify customer when fix is live (owner: maya)
eli: quick repro commands I used locally:
```
# create payload.bin with embedded nulls
printf 'header\x00middle\x00tail' > payload.bin
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tools/file_inspect \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data-binary @payload.bin
```
maya: thanks — I've told the customer the workaround (send base64 string) and that we're patching. Will follow up with timeline and credit. :thumbsup:
devin: keep me posted if we need to escalate to SRE/infra for hotfix rollout.
eli: ETA for SDK patches + runtime fix: 48 hours for hotfix + tests, 5 days for full release across ts/go. I'll post PRs here.
maya: appreciated. I'll update INC-1234 and loop back once eng confirms a patch.
samir: adding note — also validate tool schema validation for bytes fields to accept both base64 string and binary sentinel wrappers. This should avoid breakage in clients using raw buffers.
maya: closing loop for now, will reopen if customer sees further errors.
